Katie Zacharia worked at a Beijing law firm and calls herself a lawyer, but reporters found no record of her admission to practise in the US
Katie Zacharia, US President Donald Trump’s newly appointed White House press secretary, faces questions about her legal credentials after telling reporters on Tuesday that she passed a bar exam “when I moved to China”, without identifying the jurisdiction.
A review by the South China Morning Post of attorney registration records in New York, the District of Columbia, California, Texas and Florida found no listing for Zacharia.
Independent journalist Judd Legum separately reported finding no evidence that she had been admitted to practise law in any of the 50 US states or Washington, DC.

articles.title_orig: Kimberly Guilfoyle is out as U.S. ambassador to Greece
articles.title_zh: Kimberly Guilfoyle is out as U.S. ambassador to Greece
articles.content_orig:
It started out so well for her.
Kimberly Guilfoyle, the U.S. ambassador to Greece until she was effectively fired on live television on Tuesday when the new White House press secretary said that President Trump had asked for her resignation, was at one point engaged to Donald Trump Jr., the president’s eldest son. The couple owned a $9.7 million home in Florida, appeared at Trump rallies together and sent each other adoring posts on Instagram.
“Falling in love with my fiancé more and more every day,” Ms. Guilfoyle posted on Instagram on Valentine’s Day 2022. “@donaldjtrumpjr, you’re my best friend, my support system and my forever guy.”
“Thanks for always being there no matter what the haters are throwing our way,” he posted in 2024. “I love you.”
Today, the junior Mr. Trump is married to a Florida socialite and model. And Ms. Guilfoyle, who was nominated as ambassador to Greece by the president soon after her engagement to his son was broken off two years ago, is out of a job after a series of damning reports in The Wall Street Journal, including that she asked a Republican donor to pay off $100,000 on her American Express credit card just before her Senate confirmation hearing in July 2025.
The rise and fall of Ms. Guilfoyle, 57, was not a surprise at the White House, where many saw her as a flamboyant party girl with questionable judgment.
Her supporters said she was in fact a substantive person underneath the glitz. Ms. Guilfoyle, a former Fox News host and a former prosecutor in San Francisco and Los Angeles, was once married to Gavin Newsom, who would go on to become governor of California and one of the Democratic Party’s most outspoken critics of Mr. Trump.

articles.title_orig: Goldman says investors are looking for 'profitable' Chinese business growth overseas
articles.title_zh: Goldman says investors are looking for 'profitable' Chinese business growth overseas
articles.content_orig:
BEIJING — Equity investors are skeptical of Chinese companies' rapid expansion overseas, according to Goldman Sachs.
The "market wants to look for profitable expansions," Trina Chen, co-head of Greater China equity research at Goldman Sachs Research, said on a podcast that the investment bank published Tuesday.
Sluggish consumer demand in China has pushed many companies, such as electric car brands, to accelerate plans for entering other countries. Automaker Geely is one of the latest Chinese companies to push further abroad, announcing Friday it plans to enter Canada next year .
Chinese companies' overseas market share will likely reach 31% by 2035, up from around 18%, Chen and her team predicted in a Sept. 14 report. Their analysis covered more than 10 sectors, including express delivery, industrial robots and so-called white goods such as air conditioners.
Chinese businesses often find higher profit margins abroad than they would at home, enabling the companies to charge lower prices than local competitors.
Investors need to be convinced the global expansion "does not end up with something similar to involution, where the price actually gets killed because of competition," Chen said Tuesday, adding that geopolitics and market access restrictions also weighs on stock performance.
Involution refers to race-to-the-bottom competition in China, which regulators have attempted to address in recent years.
That uncertainty means Chinese companies have very little of their global expansion opportunity priced into their stocks, Chen said.
But on the flip side, she noted that investors are "ruthless" when incumbent companies lose their market share: A 10% to 15% loss could shrink market capitalization by 50% to 80%.
The Chinese players are not just looking at the U.S. and Europe. Goldman Sachs noted some of the most rapid growth is in emerging markets, as the businesses also pursue areas underserved by competitors.
"Chinese brands are no longer simply market challengers," Euromonitor said in a report last month. "Brands are becoming long-term, embedded competitors capable of reshaping market dynamics across Latin America.

articles.title_orig: 210-million-year-old dinosaur discovery reveals a lost world in Africa
articles.title_zh: 210-million-year-old dinosaur discovery reveals a lost world in Africa
articles.content_orig:
Africa boasts up to 25% of Earth’s animal and plant species . This diversity is driven by diverse habitats: harsh deserts, vast grasslands, dense forests, towering mountains, lush coastlines and teeming seas. It is also due to deep evolutionary roots, as many animal and plant groups originated here in the distant past. Paleontologists have been excavating this material for nearly two centuries .
Africa is most famous for spectacular hominid fossils that reveal our own ancestry. However, the continent boasts many fabulous fossil finds, including those of the most familiar extinct animals – dinosaurs.
The first African dinosaur fossils to be noted scientifically hailed from the Eastern Cape, South Africa and were described in the 1850s. Since then, the African dinosaur map has expanded, with rich fossil beds in South Africa, Lesotho, Tanzania, Egypt, Niger, Malawi, Madagascar and Morocco.
Zimbabwe is an important part of the African dinosaur puzzle, with dinosaur bones reported since 1916 .
As a specialist on early dinosaurs who has worked on similar material from China, the UK and Africa, I’ve been drawn to these Zimbabwean fossils to see what they reveal about the first stages of their evolution.
Our latest addition to the Triassic zoo, Musango matusadonaensis , is a sauropodomorph dinosaur. (That’s the dinosaur subgroup that eventually gave rise to four-legged, long-necked giants like Diplodocus .)
Its incomplete skeleton was found in the bank of the Nyamasango River close to Musango Island, as captured in the animal’s scientific name. Musango ’s anatomy shows us that it was bipedal (walking on its hind legs only), reached about 4.5 meters in length, and weighed 220kg. Growth marks in its bones reveal that it was a subadult when it died. Sadly, the skull wasn’t preserved, so its diet is unknown, but its close relatives were largely herbivorous (plant-eating).
Our new work reveals something unexpected about Zimbabwean dinosaurs. They’re not simply an extension of better-known South African faunas but include an array of species unique to the region. We’re now trying to work out why these differences exist. We suspect that environmental conditions might be the key.
Early fossil finds in Zimbabwe were overlooked by many scientists and it was not until the 1970s that they became more generally known . This was thanks to pioneering work by Zimbabwean paleontologists Geoffrey Bond and Michael Raath, who discovered abundant material in the hinterlands of Bulawayo (south-west Zimbabwe) and the lower Zambezi Valley (forming the border with Zambia). Most of these finds were identified as belonging to known species named from neighboring South Africa.
Paleontological work in Zimbabwe stalled for a few decades. However, a band of devoted fossil hunters kept searching. One of them, Steve Edwards, a local safari camp manager, found new, productive sites on the shore of Lake Kariba, the artificial lake which forms most of the border between Zimbabwe and Zambia. News of the discoveries eventually reached Jonah Choiniere at the University of the Witwatersrand, Johannesburg. Jonah, an expert on early dinosaurs, immediately recognized the importance of the material. He assembled an international team of South African, Zimbabwean and UK-based collaborators to explore them further.
This was a major task, as the sites on Late Kariba’s shoreline are deep inside Matusadona National Park. Our solution was to use one of the Kariba houseboats as a mobile hotel and laboratory, so that we could prospect the shoreline. We mounted two expeditions, in 2017 and 2018. We have been cleaning and studying this material ever since.
Both trips yielded a trove of material, collected from brick-red mudstones and sandstones that were laid down by ancient rivers around 210 million years ago, during the Late Triassic period (237-201 million years ago) . Geological evidence and plant fossils show that the Triassic landscape of Kariba was dry and dotted with stands of large conifer trees, with green corridors of vegetation following permanent watercourses.
Sauropodomorphs are the most common Late Triassic dinosaurs. But what’s interesting about Musango and its relative Musankwa (which we described from the same beds in 2024) is that they are unique to Zimbabwe.
We’d expected to find South African dinosaur species in these beds, given their similar age and geographic proximity, but surprisingly all the material we’ve collected so far has revealed animals that are distinct from those elsewhere.
These Zimbabwean dinosaurs are not even the closest relatives of their South African neighbors. We’ve also found other fossil animals, including lungfish and aquatic reptiles called phytosaurs, which are rare or absent in South African sites.
Following this, we’ve started to reappraise the historical dinosaur collections in Bulawayo. It appears that many of these fossils can’t be referred to South African species either, contrary to earlier assumptions.
Then, as now, Zimbabwe was further north than South Africa and closer to the equator, so climatic differences might be responsible for these varied casts of characters (as climate is known to have a strong effect on the distributions of living animals). To probe this further, we’ll be going back to Kariba in search of more fossils.
We’ll also collect more information on the exact ages and environments of these dinosaur-bearing rocks, to compare them more precisely with sites elsewhere. Although the significance of these dinosaurs is only just coming to light, Zimbabwe is already taking a greater role in shedding much needed light on early dinosaur evolution.
Materials provided by The Conversation . Original written by Paul Barrett, Individual Merit Researcher, Natural History Museum. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.

articles.title_orig: Pennsylvania at the center of US measles outbreaks
articles.title_zh: Pennsylvania at the center of US measles outbreaks
articles.content_orig:
A 39-year-old unvaccinated woman in Franklin County, Pennsylvania, has become the sixth person to die of the highly infectious virus amid a state outbreak that has stricken over a thousand people since it began in April.
The woman died on Saturday, October 10. She had several underlying health conditions and had recently tested positive for measles, according to an advisory posted on social media by Franklin County Coroner Jordan Conner. The advisory noted that the woman’s death meets the definition of a measles death set by the state’s health department.
In an emailed statement to The Washington Post , the coroner’s office said the primary cause of death was listed as “probable acute cardiac event due to possible complications of the measles.”
The previous five deaths amid the state’s measles outbreak included a newborn , a 6-week-old , an 18-year-old , a 20-year-old , and a 40-year-old . All the deceased were unvaccinated; the two infants were too young to have been vaccinated.
As of the latest measles update from Pennsylvania’s health department on Friday, October 9, there have been 1,136 cases in the state since the start of the year—1,124 of which are from the current outbreak. Overall, 218 people have been hospitalized. The outbreak, which now spans 41 of the state’s 67 counties, shows no signs of slowing. There had been 157 new cases reported just in the previous week.
A spokesperson for the state health department told the Post that it is “aware” of the new death and is reviewing the case. It will provide an update once the review is complete.
Measles, declared eliminated in the US in 2000, is roaring back amid misinformation and slipping vaccination rates. The nationwide measles case count for the year has hit 4,080 , the highest total since 1991. Pennsylvania’s outbreak is also the largest on record since that year . The US is widely expected to lose its measles elimination status when experts from the Pan American Health Organization (PAHO) meet in November to review US measles data.
Under anti-vaccine Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr., the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention has only included two of the six deaths so far in its reporting. There were three measles deaths reported in the US in 2025. Prior to those deaths, there had not been a measles death reported in the country since 2015.

articles.title_orig: American Amplifier Technologies Acquires ERI
articles.title_zh: American Amplifier Technologies Acquires ERI
articles.content_orig:
Update your browser to view this website correctly. Update my browser now
Home › News and Business › Headlines
Electronics Research Inc. has a new owner.
American Amplifier Technologies LLC, which in recent years has purchased several familiar broadcast companies including Shively Labs and Kathrein-Scala, now has acquired majority ownership of ERI from Tom Silliman.
The terms were not disclosed.
Silliman, its president/CEO since 1977, is retiring.
ERI designs, manufactures and installs broadcast antennas, towers, transmission line, filters and combiners.
AAT owner Steve Wilde told Radio World that he will continue its products and operations, including its facility in Chandler, Ind. ERI customers, he said, should expect continuity in service, support and business relationships, and can continue communicating with their contacts through existing channels.
“The acquisition is intended to strengthen ERI by providing additional resources, expanded capabilities and continued investment in the company’s long-term success,” he said.
He highlighted ERI’s significant market share in broadcast antennas and said its other offerings compliment AAT’s business. He noted the companies’ combined engineering, manufacturing, RF laboratory analysis, field-service and installation capabilities.
“We see tremendous opportunity in ERI. It has a long-standing reputation for producing proven, high-quality products and has earned the loyalty and trust of its customers.”
ERI, he continued, has “an exceptional facility, a highly capable structural steel division and extensive engineering expertise. What truly sets ERI apart is its unique combination of manufacturing capabilities and an installation division. Few companies in the industry can offer this level of expertise and capability.”
AAT makes and carries a diverse line of RF products. Wilde founded the company in 2008, along with sister firm SWE Services.
Over the past seven years he has been active at seeking acquisition opportunities.
In 2019 AAT acquired Mauna Towers, which operates tower facilities in Hawaii and Arizona. In 2023, it purchased antenna and filter manufacturer Shively Labs and also started a partnership with System Engineering Solutions . Then in late 2025, AAT acquired Kathrein Broadcast USA , also known as Kathrein-Scala.
AAT is based in Citrus Heights near Sacramento, Calif. Kathrein-Scala continues to run out of White City near Medford, Ore. [Read a history of AAT .]
“ERI, Shively and Kathrein-Scala are names that generations of broadcast engineers know and trust,” Wilde said.
“We recognize the responsibility that comes with bringing companies with those histories together. We intend to protect what makes each of these companies special while giving the personnel and technologies new opportunities to grow.”
Electronics Research Inc. was founded during World War II, making antennas for military aircraft. Later moving into broadcasting, its innovations have included the Rototiller antenna line, the Lambda optimized FM mounting system and Cogwheel master FM antennas.
In 2003 ERI acquired Andrew Corp.’s Broadcast Products business, including its television antenna products, rigid transmission-line products and related broadcast RF components.
Wilde called ERI “an exceptional company with a remarkable history.”
ERI’s headquarters and main manufacturing facility include over 100,000 square feet of manufacturing, design and office space. The facility also houses a 70,000-cubic-foot anechoic chamber, which according to ERI’s website is the largest of its kind in North America. [Read a history of ERI .]
The Silliman name has long been associated with ERI. Robert Silliman was involved with the company from its earliest years, eventually becoming one of its owners. Tom joined the company in 1969 and became president/CEO in 1977. Robert received the NAB Engineering Achievement Award in 1993, and Tom received it in 2008. Robert Silliman died in 2001.
“One of our primary goals is to honor Tom Silliman’s legacy by continuing his commitment to quality, engineering excellence and innovation, while expanding our capabilities to better serve the broadcast community,” Wilde said in the announcement.
Tom Silliman was quoted: “I am proud of what the people of ERI have built over the years, and I believe AAT is well positioned to carry that work forward. We share a commitment to engineering, quality, customer service and the broadcast industry.” [Read our 2001 profile of Tom Silliman .]

articles.title_orig: Atletico Madrid 2 Man Utd 0: How much pressure is Michael Carrick under now?
articles.title_zh: Atletico Madrid 2 Man Utd 0: How much pressure is Michael Carrick under now?
articles.content_orig:
Updates from nine Champions League matches
Jess Anderson, Gary Rose and Charlotte Coates
That's all from us, we'll be back tomorrow with more Champions League action.
Until then, you can read all the reports from tonight's games here and read more about Lisandro Martinez's criticism of Manchester United here .
Martinez is 100% right. The players haven't been good enough except very few. We need 23 top-class players.
It feels shocking to hear Martinez speak so openly. Those are criticisms fans have been chatting about in the pub for years - hearing it from a players mouth is staggering.
Ashley Young Former Manchester United winger on Amazon Prime
We spoke before the game on how the club needs to invest more, but when they invested in midfield they are not going to be able to go [and buy more]. What does [Martinez] want, a whole new team? They are not going to do that. They need to start in different positions. They could of brought in defence, they could of brought in front but they didn't.
He's just come off the pitch, and emotions are running high. I get and understand that, but we know the recruitment needs to work, it has to be better but it takes time and do it.
The players know that themselves and need to take it among themselves that they are the players in this squad and they are the ones on this pitch and go and produce. There won't be any changes now until you get to January.
Might be the best thing Lisandro has done in a United shirt. But the ownership are still there against the wishes of nearly every United fan, they continue to run the club the way they want (to its detriment), so thereâs no need to think Martinezâs words will move them.
Wayne Rooney Former England striker on Amazon Prime
That interview is not going to help the situation that the club is in. It's going to bring greater noise, the players are unhappy, they're unsettled and don't trust their own teammates. It's not going to help at all.
Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta speaking to TNT Sports:
"We had to increase the technical level, teams are really well organised at this level. We gave simple things away - bad touches, mis-timed things, when we sent balls into the box it was into the wrong areas and we get caught. Once we did that better we started to play in the opposition box and with the quality we have they made a difference."
On quality of substitutions: "The ones that started too, we get into some incredible positions. The ones that finished the game were extraordinary - they increased the intensity and quality.
"The minutes are given because they deserve them. Everyone has to earn it because we can see competition and options and that will only ebenfit our performances."
On preparing for the next one: "It's difficult in the Champions League - Lille are a brilliant team. But winning helps - the energy will be good when we start to prepare the Sunday game."
Arsenal winger Eberechi Eze speaking to TNT Sports:
"Good performance. We did what we needed to do. Played free and enjoyed it."
On staying patient: "That can happen here. A lot of teams come with energy so first halves can be difficult but we know that we have to grind teams down eventually. It was a good day.
"It's good fun. The type of players we're playing with you're always linking and finding space. It's enjoyable and as long as I'm doing that then I'm happy."
On squad depth: "It is difficult, every player wants to play. The mentality is always to be on the pitch, affect games and earn your place. I'm doing what I can, enjoying what I'm doing.
"Always happy to score, to affect games and be having fun on the pitch and expressing myself."
On half-time team talk: "We knew what we were doing, there were slight details to give us more chances and have more balls inside their box.
"We trust and back ourselves, we know our quality. We play games to win and believe we can and should. It's about the work we've done on the pitch."
On mentality shift from last season: "It's now a different challenge we have. We achieved something amazing last season and we want to build on that. We're coming at it at a slightly different angle but the mentality is still the same - to be ruthless and dominate as much as we can."
Wayne Rooney Former England striker on Amazon Prime
It's a bit disrespectful to his teammates too. He's saying that they are not good enough.
Paul Robinson Former England goalkeeper on BBC Radio 5 Live
On the comments from Lisandro Martinez:
I question his timing, the noise around Manchester United at the moment, positivity needs to come out of the dressing room.
But on the flip side of that I actually quite like it - a player being honest, every Manchester United fan across the country doesn't need their players coming out saying 'we're doing ok, the squad's strong enough'.
Everyone can see they didn't recruit well enough and they need more players and the squad's not strong enough.
Martinez might be correct about the people at the top not doing enough. But their lack of activity is not causing his poor performances. Solanke didnât get the better of him on Saturday because of a lack of subs. He needs to give his head a wobble.
Ian Dennis BBC Radio 5 Live senior football reporter
For Lisandro Martinez to have that clarity of thought, that strikes me as premeditated.
Thinking 'if we lose here tonight that's what I'm going to say' because otherwise you don't dig out the technical director in that circumstance.
Wow, very brave for Martinez for call out the upper management like that. I'm sure it won't go down well within Manchester United but I am also sure fans will be happy that someone in the club is finally saying it in public
Martinez is right, refreshing to hear an honest assessment. Rooney and Young being unhappy and 'should be kept in the boardroom' are so wrong, we pay their astronomical wages. We should praise the honesty, as  we all know the problems
Martinez saying what most of the fans think. The rot starts at the top, and the squad is not up to the task.  Rare honesty from a modern player!
Wayne Rooney Former England striker on Amazon Prime
I disagree [with Martinez's comments]. I thought that the performance was okay. I thought it was better, so there were some positive signs.
It's a difficult one because I always used to feel that I was outspoken as a player and you want to have your opinion.
I think he's maybe gone a bit too far, and that should have stayed internal.
The fans want to hear the players speak, they want to hear the players care so you can clearly see that he cares and he wants the club to invest more money in more players, and to do that he's probably one of the players who'll be out the door if I'm being honest.
His performances haven't been good enough, but I think in some ways he's right in terms of the club needing to invest more at the top end of the pitch and the defence, but I think it looks like it was a bit of an agenda and he wanted to say that because it doesn't reflect the performance I thought the performance was better.
Those Lisandro Martinez comments have certainly got people talking...
Paul Robinson Former England goalkeeper on BBC Radio 5 Live
VAR stay out of it, just keep your nose out. That's somebody else's opinion. It's not the referee on the field, it's somebody sat watching the television trying to referee the game.
I can completely understand it if the referee has given it on the field because he's one-on-one, there's contact, an arm across the chest.
The referee has seen it, he's on the field, he's ten yards from it. He has chosen not to give it. Don't get involved, keep out of it.
That is just what's frustrating.
Wayne Rooney Former England striker on Amazon Prime
I thought it was better tonight. Obviously the result is disappointing, but there were positive signs tonight.
I thought Baleba coming in was exellent, and he added that extra enenrgy in the middle. I thought that Santos did well in there too. Overall there were a lot more positives tonight.

58% of this demand is driven by teachers leaving the profession. Global annual attrition rates currently stand at 7.2% in pre-primary, 4.7% in primary, 5.4% in secondary education.
In 27 of the 68 countries analyzed ( list available the factsheet ) , teacher salaries remain below those of similarly qualified professionals across all education levels. The global pupil–teacher ratio in primary education is approximately 28 pupils per teacher.
UNESCO works with governments and education stakeholders to strengthen the recognition, support and conditions that enable teachers to thrive.
As Artificial Intelligence (AI) transforms education and the teaching profession, UNESCO is supporting countries in strengthening teachers’ digital and AI competencies, including through the adoption and implementation of UNESCO’s AI Competency Framework for Teachers .
The joint Ministerial Statement on Education in the Age of AI , adopted at UNESCO on 8 September 2026, emphasizes that AI must support rather than replace teachers' professional contribution and judgement. The statement calls on countries to strengthen teacher agency through investment in teacher preparation and professional development, while ensuring that teachers play an active role in decisions regarding the use of AI systems in classrooms.
What? World Teachers' Day: "Standing with teachers: 60 years of protecting the profession, advancing its status and shaping our futures"
When? Monday 5 October 2026 - 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. (CEST)
Where? UNESCO Headquarters, 125 avenue de Suffren, 75007 Paris, France
Please register here to request press accreditation for the event.
The opening session will be streamed live on the UNESCO website .
World Teachers' Day 2026 marks the 60th anniversary of the Global Recommendation concerning the Status of Teachers , a landmark international instrument setting standards for teachers' rights, responsibilities and working conditions.
To celebrate the occasion, UNESCO will bring together teachers, policymakers, and education partners from around at its Paris Headquarters on Monday 5 October (see the full programme here ). The event will feature high-level discussions on protecting and advancing the status of teachers, including a keynote speech by Gert Biesta , Professor of Education at the University of Melbourne.
The event will also include the award ceremony for the UNESCO-Hamdan Prize for Teacher Development . Supported by the Hamdan Bin Rashid Al Maktoum Foundation for Medical and Educational Sciences, the Prize awards $300,000 every two years, equally divided among the three winning organizations.
This year, ten initiatives from around the world have been selected as finalists for their work in strengthening teachers and improving teaching. The three laureates will be announced during the ceremony. Discover the ten finalists of the UNESCO-Hamdan Prize for Teacher Development .

articles.title_orig: Save The World’s Rivers submits formal Stagecoach Mountain Ranch comments to Routt County planners
articles.title_zh: Save The World’s Rivers submits formal Stagecoach Mountain Ranch comments to Routt County planners
articles.content_orig:
jcoccaro@steamboatpilot.com
Save The World’s Rivers , a Colorado-based river conservation nonprofit, has submitted formal comments to the Routt County Planning Department on Discovery Land Company’s Stagecoach Mountain Ranch application, with the organization’s remarks limited squarely to the proposed development’s impacts on water.
In a six-page comment letter dated Oct. 7 , Save The World’s Rivers Executive Director Gary Wockner asked county planners to require a comprehensive list of documents and analyses from Discovery Land Company that demonstrate full compliance with the legal standards mandated for the project.
The nonprofit’s programs, Save The Colorado and Save The Poudre, work to protect and restore rivers within the Colorado River Basin, including the Yampa River.
Stagecoach Mountain Ranch is a 6,100-acre proposed private ski area and luxury residential development near Stagecoach Reservoir in South Routt County. Plans for the development include 613 luxury units alongside 137 workforce housing units, with 95 units marked for affordable housing accessible to the public.
Wockner’s letter comes approximately two months after the Routt County Planning Department submitted its second corrections letter to Discovery Land Company on its proposal , identifying more than 120 questions, conflicts and missing materials to be resolved before the county completes its review of the project’s 10 pending land-use applications.
Wockner began the letter by stating that the applicant’s current record of adequate water supply does not meet state standards and that Discovery Land Company’s current demand figures conflict.
The Stagecoach Mountain Ranch website, he wrote, lists potable water demand of 365 acre-feet per year and snowmaking demand of 275 acre-feet per year — yet according to the Upper Yampa Water Conservancy District, the developers said in May 2025 that snowmaking would need approximately 400 acre-feet annually.
“The county should require one reconciled number, prepared by a registered engineer, before making any adequacy determination,” wrote Wockner, who added that the demand estimate “rests on an assumption the county cannot enforce.”
Discovery Land Company’s potable water estimate assumes that second homeowners occupy their homes 20-25 days a year, with demand calculated at 50% occupancy. Occupancy patterns, however, change based on ownership, remote work and short-term rentals, argued Wockner.
“If occupancy rises, demand rises with it,” he wrote. “An adequacy finding built on low occupancy is only valid if the county also caps actual use.”
On water sources, the Upper Yampa Water Conservancy District, wrote Wockner, states that it has not received an application for a storage contract, and that no infrastructure currently exists to deliver reservoir water to the location of the ski area.
“The county should require a hydrogeologic analysis of the Browns Park wells, including whether the water is tributary to the Yampa and, if so, how depletions will be replace,” he wrote.
Drought conditions are the test for water supply, Wockner added — not the exception.
He requested that county planners require a reconciled report modeling dry-year yield, condition any approval on binding annual and daily caps for potable and snowmaking use, and require meters, public annual reporting and “mandatory curtailment of snowmaking in dry years.”
Wockner noted that as of Jan. 1, per state law, the county cannot allow the installation or placement of “nonfunctional turf, artificial turf or invasive plants in new development on commercial, institutional, industrial or common-interest-community property.”
The Stagecoach Mountain Ranch commercial base area, its proposed community marketplace and homeowners association-owned common areas, he said, fall within that prohibition.
Wockner referred to comments submitted by the Western Resilience Center in mid-September , which cites noteworthy commitments in Discovery Land Company’s sustainability plan and climate action plan strategy for the development.
Like Western Resilience, Save The World’s Rivers wonders to what extent they will become a “binding and enforceable component” of the final design and operation.
“Unless the County writes them into the approval, they will not,” wrote Wockner, who asked the county to convert every conservation commitment into a condition of approval, plat note and recorded covenant naming Routt County as a third-party beneficiary with enforcement rights.
Wockner was particularly blunt on the issue of water quality in Stagecoach Reservoir.
“Stagecoach Reservoir is not a healthy baseline that (Stagecoach Mountain Ranch) might degrade,” he wrote. “It is already in trouble.”
According to a 2025 monitoring report from the Upper Yampa Water Conservancy District, chlorophyll-a at every reservoir site from late August through November 2025 exceeded both the cold-water aquatic life and direct-use water supply standards.
Cyanobacteria in the reservoir peaked between 50,000-60,000 cells/mL in September 2025, a level the report associated with “moderate-to-high recreational health risk,” with the bacteria’s dominant genus capable of producing toxins.
Additionally, the Yampa River immediately above and below the reservoir is on the state’s list of impaired waters for temperature.
“The wastewater plant is the crux,” wrote Wockner. All sewage from Stagecoach Mountain Ranch would go to the Morrison Creek Metropolitan Water and Sanitation District’s plant, which discharges directly into the reservoir.
Wockner noted that the plant’s discharge permit, issued in 2015, has expired, and that its renewal must account for effluent standards adopted since 2015.
Save The World’s Rivers is requesting a permit renewal that meets current standards; a phased schedule tying plat approvals to completed and funded wastewater capacity such that “units never outrun treatment”; and a binding “no net increase” nutrient commitment for total phosphorus and nitrogen reaching the reservoir, verified by applicant-funded monitoring conducted by either the district or a third party.
The nonprofit is further requesting a long-term performance guarantee that would compel Stagecoach Mountain Ranch to fund and execute remediation should reservoir water quality degrade — backed by escrowed funds and a revenue-based impact fund — as well as the prohibition of treated effluent in snowmaking, noted as illegal in Colorado.
Wockner joined Western Resilience in asking the county to strictly apply its “unavoidable encroachment” provision, noting that any encroachment should be presumed avoidable and that the applicant should bear the burden of proving otherwise.
The project website states that Discovery Land Company’s stormwater measures will cut phosphorus by 50-70% and nitrogen by 55%, and promises monitoring. Such figures should serve as enforceable performance standards, argued Wockner — not marketing.
“The applicant claims snowmaking on north-facing slopes will deliver colder water later in the melt season,” wrote Wockner. “That is a hypothesis, not a finding.”
Snowmaking, he continued, also loses water to evaporation and sublimation. He suggested the county require a hydrologic analysis of how snowmaking diversions and altered melt timing could affect flows and temperature in the relevant segments of the Yampa River.
“The Upper Yampa is already telling us its limits. The tailwater has been closed to fishing since October 2025,” wrote Wockner at the close of his comments. “The river above and below the dam is listed as impaired.”
“Into this system, SMR proposes roughly 750 residences, a private ski area with snowmaking, and a wastewater load that the existing plant cannot carry at buildout,” he continued.
Routt County, Wockner wrote, must “make every promise of conservation and water-quality protection binding, funded and enforceable before the first plat is recorded.” If Discovery Land Company cannot meet such standards, the county, he

articles.title_orig: Zelensky and Burnham to meet in Downing Street
articles.title_zh: Zelensky and Burnham to meet in Downing Street
articles.content_orig:
Prime Minister Andy Burnham will host Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky at Downing Street on Wednesday, as the UK announces it will accelerate its delivery of air defence missiles to Kyiv.
Burnham is also expected to set out how his government will draw up further sanctions against Russia.
Speaking ahead of the meeting, Burnham said the UK was with Ukraine "for as long as it takes", adding: "Russian aggression cannot be allowed to succeed on our continent."
The UK will also urge allies to step up pressure on Russia, with Chancellor John Healey using International Monetary Fund (IMF) meetings to call for a ban on Russian liquefied natural gas (LNG).
This will be Zelensky's second visit to the UK since Burnham became prime minister. His first was in late July, days after Burnham entered No 10, when the pair met troops and led a news conference at a naval base in Portsmouth.
Burnham said: "Our rock-solid support to Ukraine is vital for keeping us safe here in the UK and ensuring those on the frontlines have the equipment they need to push back Russia.
"My message to the Ukrainian people could not be clearer, we are with you for as long as it takes, and we will go further and faster in our support to back your courageous fight for peace in Europe.
"It is not just the right thing to do, but it's the necessary thing to do."
Among the measures being announced is the quicker delivery of British Lightweight Multirole Missiles (LMMs), with the UK having already committed to send more than 5,000 worth £1.6bn over the next four years.
The UK will also reaffirm its plans to fully implement a maritime services ban on Russian LNG exports.
The meeting between Zelensky and Burnham follows what Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband described as a "very difficult few days" for UK-US relations due to President Donald Trump's decision to ease sanctions on Russian diesel.
Zelensky criticised the US deal with Russia, calling it a "gift" to President Vladimir Putin. Trump, in response, called for new leadership in Ukraine and criticised Zelensky for striking Russian oil refineries.
Meanwhile, Healey will ask partners at the IMF to step up support for Kyiv and ensure Russia heeds the US' call for a full energy ceasefire.
Trump claimed on Sunday that Russia and Ukraine had agreed to an immediate energy ceasefire - but hours later, Zelensky said Russian attacks on energy facilities had continued.
On Monday, Russia's Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov said Ukraine did not deserve the "respite" a ceasefire would bring.

articles.title_orig: Measles case reported in Huntsville
articles.title_zh: Measles case reported in Huntsville
articles.content_orig:
HUNTSVILLE, Ala. ( WAFF ) - Alabama health officials are warning the public after a case of measles was reported in Huntsville involving an international traveler who visited businesses in the Bailey Cove area while infectious.
The Alabama Department of Public Health says a private lab reported the positive test and is now urging anyone who may have been exposed to check their vaccine status and watch for symptoms.
Health officials say the person visited these locations:
Subway, 7900 Bailey Cove Road in Huntsville, on Oct. 4, 5 and 7 between 11:30 a.m. and 3 p.m.
Publix at 12796 Bailey Cove Road Southeast, on Oct. 4 between 1 and 3 p.m.
ADPH advises anyone who was at the restaurant or store during those times to check their vaccine status and monitor for measles symptoms.
Wes Stubblefield with the ADPH said measles is a highly infectious virus.
“Individuals should, if they were in proximity or in those establishments at that time, they should monitor themselves for symptoms,” Stubblefield said. “And if they have any symptoms that might be concerning for a measles illness, that they notify their local physician or any clinic that they present to before they go. Tell them that they are concerned that they may have been in contact and may have symptoms concerning for measles.”
Measles is a serious, highly contagious viral respiratory illness that spreads through droplets in the air when someone with measles coughs or sneezes.
If exposed, unvaccinated people have a 90% chance of becoming infected. Symptoms usually appear 7 to 14 days after infection, and infected people can spread it to others for several days before showing symptoms.
Health officials say the best way to protect yourself is to get the measles-mumps-rubella, or MMR, vaccine.
The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention has reported more than 4,000 confirmed measles cases in the U.S. this year. Many cases originate from international travel.
Anyone traveling internationally should be fully vaccinated before traveling. Infants 6 to 11 months old should get one dose before travel, then two more doses after their first birthday.
Measles can cause serious complications, especially in children under 5, including ear infections, diarrhea, pneumonia, swelling of the brain and even death. Parents should make sure their children are up to date on routine immunizations. Adults unsure of their status should contact their health care provider.

articles.title_orig: Trump debates calling off livestream of firing squad execution after learning Fort Hood shooter was paralyzed
articles.title_zh: Trump debates calling off livestream of firing squad execution after learning Fort Hood shooter was paralyzed
articles.content_orig:
President Donald Trump and his advisers are debating whether to call off plans to livestream the firing squad execution of the Fort Hood shooter, with Trump having remarked privately that he did not initially know that Nidal Hasan was paralyzed from the waist down, two sources familiar with the discussions told CNN.
The president was not aware that Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth was announcing last week that the administration planned to let the public watch the execution, the sources said, and was not sure what to make of it at first. Trump was, however, firmly behind the decision to execute Hasan via firing squad , multiple officials told CNN, and he’s often defended it in public.
And even after Hegseth posted on X on Thursday confirming that the Pentagon planned to livestream the execution, Trump polled several of his advisers and allies about how to proceed.
It was during the those conversations that Trump learned Hasan was paralyzed from the waist down — he was shot in the back by law enforcement during the 2009 shooting at Ford Hood — and that he now uses a wheelchair, the sources said, which made showing the execution publicly less palatable to the president.
One of the sources familiar with the discussions pointed to Trump’s deep understanding of imagery as a key reason why he may decide to ditch plans for the livestream. The president has also listened to the argument that a public execution by firing squad could serve as propaganda for foreign adversaries and terrorists to try to paint Hasan as a martyr, a Trump adviser told CNN.
The White House on Tuesday referred CNN to the president’s comments on Saturday in which he acknowledged “two thoughts” about what to do and said he’d make the ultimate decision.
“He was vicious. He was violent,” Trump told reporters about Hasan over the weekend. “There are two thoughts: Don’t show it and show it. Because, you know, by showing it, maybe other people won’t be doing what he did. So, I’ll make a decision ultimately. I know what the military would like to do, but we’ll make a decision.”
The Pentagon is also reevaluating plans to fully livestream the execution, according to a source familiar with the discussions. Even if there is a broadcast of the event, the source said, it will likely be cut before shots are fired, in part, due to concerns that the moment could offer a propaganda opportunity for terrorist groups.
Hegseth’s office has not responded to additional requests for comment about whether plans to livestream the execution have changed.
The plan to livestream the execution has faced bipartisan backlash, and people across the Pentagon and the Army were caught off guard, CNN has previously reported .
Trump told reporters on Friday that he was not involved but said, “I understand the decision,” adding that some people “want to set an example” by livestreaming the execution.
Hegseth had initially recommended death by firing squad for Hasan — who was convicted of killing 13 people and wounding dozens of others — and Trump approved it.
The execution, which is scheduled for December 3 at Fort Hood, would be the US Army’s first such execution of a soldier since World War II and its first imposition of any death penalty on an armed service member in 65 years.
A US-born citizen of Palestinian descent, Hasan said he was targeting soldiers he was set to deploy with to Afghanistan and wanted to protect the Taliban and its leaders from the US military.
CNN’s Zachary Cohen contributed to this report.

articles.title_orig: Congo's confirmed Ebola cases exceed 9,000 as containment efforts falter - ABC News
articles.title_zh: Congo's confirmed Ebola cases exceed 9,000 as containment efforts falter - ABC News
articles.source: Breaking News, Latest News and Videos
articles.content_orig:
Confirmed Ebola cases have surpassed 9,000 in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) outbreak, according to Health Ministry data, as efforts to stifle transmission falter.
The ministry reported 9,066 confirmed cases and 4,381 deaths on Tuesday – a death toll of nearly half the known cases.
The outbreak, caused by the Bundibugyo strain of Ebola, has become the largest and deadliest in the DRC’s history. Globally, the toll is only second to the 2014 to 2016 West African epidemic, which saw 28,600 confirmed cases and more than 11,000 deaths across Guinea, ⁠⁠Liberia and Sierra Leone, according to the World Health Organization (WHO).
The Bundibugyo strain currently has no approved vaccines or treatments and has raised concerns over cross-border transmission.
Last week, Kenya reported its first imported case in which a Kenyan national who lived in the DRC travelled through Uganda before reaching Nairobi, where he died.
Uganda also reported 20 cases and two deaths earlier in the year, but the country was declared Ebola-free in August.
The current outbreak in the DRC was announced in mid-May, but some experts suspect it began as early as February. The virus, which is transmitted through contact with bodily fluids, has spread to seven provinces in the north and east.
Efforts to contain the virus face obstacles as health workers and other responders in the DRC face mistrust in local communities, with many believing the disease is a ruse for officials to siphon off money . The outbreak is also occurring amid an ongoing conflict between the M23 rebel group and government forces, making transport of healthcare resources to remote regions difficult.
A local politician in eastern DRC was beaten to death in September after he defended the government’s Ebola response on the radio, according to his political party.
A clinical trial to evaluate vaccine efficacy against the Bundibugyo strain is being prepared for the DRC in the coming weeks, WHO Health Emergencies Programme Executive Director Dr Chikwe Ihekweazu said on Tuesday.

articles.title_orig: Real-World, First-Line IO-Based Combos Are Associated With Improved OS vs TKI Monotherapy in Advanced RCC
articles.title_zh: Real-World, First-Line IO-Based Combos Are Associated With Improved OS vs TKI Monotherapy in Advanced RCC
articles.content_orig:
First-line IO-based combination regimens were increasingly used and associated with longer observed survival in advanced renal cell carcinoma.
First-line immuno-oncology (IO)–based combination regimens, particularly IO plus a TKI, were associated with improved overall survival (OS) compared with TKI monotherapy in a real-world cohort of patients with advanced renal cell carcinoma (RCC), according to findings from a retrospective real-world study presented at the 2026 Kidney Cancer Research Summit . 1,2
Findings showed that at a median follow-up of 13.9 months, the median OS in the overall population (n = 2123) was 34.7 months. 1 Notably, the median OS was 44.1 months among patients who received an IO-TKI combination (n = 987) compared with 32.8 months for those given an IO-IO combination (n = 746) and 29.8 months for patients given TKI monotherapy (n = 390).
Notably, from 2019 to 2024, the proportion of patients receiving an IO-TKI combination increased from 33.8% to 48.6%, whereas IO-IO decreased from 40.5% to 34.5% and TKI monotherapy decreased from 25.7% to 16.9%.
“The advanced RCC treatment landscape continues to evolve toward IO-based combinations in [the] first line and continued TKI monotherapy in later lines,” lead study author Neil J. Shah, MBBS, and colleagues wrote in the poster. “While health care resource utilization [HCRU] and costs remain substantial, these results underscore both the clinical progress achieved and the ongoing opportunity to optimize resource use in advanced RCC care.”
Shah is an assistant attending physician and genitourinary medical oncologist at Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center in New York, New York.
Investigators conducted a retrospective cohort study using Optum’s deidentified Clinformatics Data Mart Database, with the database period extended from January 1, 2017, through December 31, 2024, and included commercially insured and Medicare Advantage beneficiaries.
Eligible adults had at least 2 claims with an RCC diagnosis, evidence of secondary metastasis, and initiation of a National Comprehensive Cancer Network–recommended first-line systemic regimen on or after April 19, 2019. Patients were categorized according to whether they received IO-TKI, IO-IO, or TKI monotherapy.
Investigators evaluated outcomes included treatment patterns, treatment sequencing, OS, all-cause and advanced RCC–related HCRU, and costs. OS was estimated using an unadjusted Kaplan-Meier analysis, and HCRU and costs were calculated on a per-patient-per-month (PPPM) basis.
The mean age of the overall population was 68.1 years (standard deviation [SD], 9.6), and the median age was 69.0 years (interquartile range [IQR], 63.0-75.0). The respective mean ages were 67.4, 68.2, and 69.5 years in the IO-TKI, IO-IO, and TKI monotherapy groups. Men comprised 70.9% of the overall population, including 71.6%, 72.8%, and 65.6% of the respective treatment cohorts.
Overall, 50.2% of patients were non-Hispanic White, 7.3% were non-Hispanic Black, 13.6% were Hispanic, and 2.2% were Asian; race or ethnicity was unknown for 26.7% of patients. Most patients lived in the South (45.1%), followed by the Midwest (25.1%), West (19.5%), and Northeast (10.3%).
Medicare Advantage covered 71.1% of the study population, and 28.9% had commercial insurance. The proportion covered by Medicare Advantage was highest in the TKI-monotherapy group at 78.7%, compared with 71.0% in the IO-IO group and 68.1% in the IO-TKI group.
Additional data showed that 32.3% of patients remained on their initial treatment, 29.0% advanced to second-line therapy, and 18.7% died. Another 20.0% discontinued treatment without a recorded death or subsequent therapy.
TKI monotherapy was the most frequently used treatment class in both the second- and third-line settings. Among patients who received second-line therapy, 47.2% received TKI monotherapy compared with 23.1% who received IO-TKI, 9.3% who received IO monotherapy, 7.6% who received a TKI plus an mTOR inhibitor, 7.0% who received IO-IO, and 5.8% who received another regimen.
In the third-line setting, 42.1% of patients received TKI monotherapy, 18.8% received IO-TKI, and 14.2% received a TKI plus an mTOR inhibitor; other treatments were administered to 15.2% of patients.
Overall, 61.3% of patients had at least 1 inpatient admission, including 57.6% treated with first-line IO-TKI, 66.6% treated with IO-IO, and 60.5% treated with TKI monotherapy. The median PPPM inpatient admissions was 0.1 overall. Median lengths of stay were 1.0 day with IO-TKI, 1.1 days with IO-IO, and 1.3 days with TKI monotherapy.
At least 1 emergency department visit was reported for 64.1% of patients, whereas 99.8% had at least 1 outpatient visit. The median number of outpatient visits PPPM was 5.4 overall, including 5.5 with IO-TKI, 5.6 with IO-IO, and 4.3 with TKI monotherapy.
Median total health care costs PPPM were $32,829 overall, $38,408 with IO-TKI, $30,484 with IO-IO, and $24,098 with TKI monotherapy.
Median medical costs PPPM were highest with IO-IO at $26,589, compared with $21,800 for IO-TKI and $7462 for TKI monotherapy. Conversely, median pharmacy costs were $15,871 with IO-TKI, $15,103 with TKI monotherapy, and $415 with IO-IO. Investigators noted that the oral administration of TKIs may have contributed to higher pharmacy costs, whereas intravenously administered IO agents may have contributed to higher medical costs.

articles.title_zh: China Spooked Memory Stocks. Investors Picked Their Losers.
articles.content_orig:
Oops, something went wrong
Our analysts just identified a stock with the potential to be the next Nvidia. Tell us how you invest and we'll show you why it's our #1 pick. Tap here.
China rattled the memory trade on Tuesday. But by the close, investors had made up their minds about who actually has a problem. It's the DRAM makers.
ChangXin Memory Technologies, China's biggest memory chipmaker, said over the weekend it had made real progress on a new chip design that crams more data into less space, CNBC reports. Asia took it badly: SK Hynix plunged more than 10% in Seoul and Samsung fell over 7%.
U.S. memory stocks opened in the same hole, with nearly every name down 5% to 8%. Then the buyers showed up.
Seagate, Western Digital and SanDisk clawed back almost all of it and closed down less than 2%. Micron didn't get the same rescue. It finished down 3.6%, its second straight loss. SK Hynix's U.S. shares fell 3.2%. The S&P 500 ended flat.
One stock. Nvidia-level potential. 30M+ investors trust Moby to find it first. Get the pick. Tap here.
The split makes sense. CXMT makes DRAM, the same chips Micron, SK Hynix and Samsung sell. A Chinese rival closing the gap is a direct shot at their pricing. Hard drives and flash storage are a different business.
Some analysts think the market overreacted. Rayliant's Phillip Wool told CNBC that CXMT still hasn't shown it can produce at scale, and it isn't a threat yet in the high-bandwidth memory chips that power AI. He said the selloff showed "how vulnerable AI sentiment is at this moment."
Still, the CXMT news looks more like an excuse than a cause. Memory stocks were already well off their highs before the weekend, with Micron down about a quarter from its peak and Western Digital down by half. Investors have been hunting for a reason to take profits on the AI trade's biggest winners. China handed them one, and they used it on the stocks with the most to lose.

articles.title_orig: A Father’s Mission Is to Show the World ‘What Russia Did to My Family’
articles.title_zh: A Father’s Mission Is to Show the World ‘What Russia Did to My Family’
articles.content_orig:
Russian President Vladimir Putin and U.S. President Donald Trump at Joint Base Elmendorf-Richardson in Alaska on Aug. 15, 2025.
President Donald Trump is facing growing backlash over his plan to import diesel from Russia , with some Republican and Democratic lawmakers insisting that the controversial deal “violates” the law.
Congress four years ago passed the Ending Importation of Russian Oil Act , which prohibits U.S. imports of Russian-origin energy products covered by Chapter 27 of the Harmonized Tariff Schedule , including diesel. Democratic Rep. Lloyd Doggett of Texas, the bill's chief sponsor, argued Monday that Trump is “directly violating that law” by “lifting sanctions to permit the first Russian diesel imports into the United States since the law took effect, without satisfying the specific legal conditions it requires.”
He suggested the lack of congressional oversight on Trump’s deal with Putin renders it unlawful, and noted how the plan showcases a sharp turn from Washington, as it comes just weeks after Trump signed a sweeping Russia sanctions bill intended to target the country's financial institutions and the energy industry, which has largely financed the assault on Ukraine. The sanctions bill was named after Lindsey Graham, the late Republican Senator who spent the final year of his life building support for the measure.
“Russia can [now] export fossil fuel to the U.S. after Trump violated the specific provisions of a federal statute,” Doggett said on Tuesday in a statement to TIME. “While offering little benefit for Americans, this unlawful action will provide substantial new funding for Putin‘s war machine to continue murdering Ukrainian civilians.”
Doggett’s concerns match those of Republican Sen. Thom Tillis of North Carolina, who told NBC’s Meet the Press over the weekend that he believes “there’s a legitimate case for saying the President’s not following the law.”
Tillis was one of seven Senators who publicly urged the Administration on Sunday to “immediately reverse course” on the agreement announced Friday, arguing that it goes against the 2022 law.
“Congress explicitly banned Russian energy imports in 2022 to prevent American dollars from financing Putin’s brutal war against Ukraine,” read the statement co-signed by Republican Senators Lisa Murkowski of Alaska, Susan Collins of Maine, Thom Tillis of North Carolina, and John Curtis of Utah, alongside Democratic Senators Jeanne Shaheen of New Hampshire, Ron Wyden of Oregon, and Richard Blumenthal of Connecticut.
“President Trump’s decision to allow Russian diesel imports to the U.S. runs directly counter to that law. The Administration has also failed to consult with Congress or submit any explanation to justify its decision as required by statute,” they said.
In a letter sent to Trump on Tuesday, Tillis, Collins, and Murkowski, were joined by fellow Republican Senators Mitch McConnell of Kentucky, John Cornyn of Texas, and Alan Armstrong of Oklahoma alongside six Democratic Senators as they told the President the deal “is a gift to our adversary and a betrayal of our Allies [and] should be rescinded.” The letter came a day after Trump publicly dismissed the criticism stemming from within his own party.
"Well, I think these are Republicans that can't really be serious," he told reporters at the White House. “Anything that could help our farmers, our ranchers, I like.”
Trump’s deal to "immediately" supply 300,000 tons of diesel to American and global markets comes as he faces growing political pressure ahead of the November midterms. Spiraling energy costs have become a key concern for voters, threatening to undermine Republican efforts to maintain their majorities in Congress. The financial upheaval has meant that Trump risks losing his hold on farm country . However, experts are skeptical that an influx of Russian fuel will bring relief to struggling Americans, given how short the supply is due to the disruption in the Strait of Hormuz.
While some lawmakers also predict the impact on American consumers will be slight , the key sticking point for many centers on whether Trump’s diesel deal with Putin violates the 2022 law, with some Republicans and Democrats insisting that Trump is pushing the limits of presidential authority. Here’s what to know about the debate—and where legal experts stand on the matter.
While Presidents typically have broad authority to waive sanctions, Congress placed specific limits on that power in the April 2022 legislation, says Kristen Eichensehr, a professor of law at Harvard Law School.
“In many sanctions authorities, the President has broad authority to waive imposition of the sanctions or to issue licenses that basically provide an exception to the sanctions,” she tells TIME. “The [2022 act] is an unusual law, given how careful and specific Congress was in providing that the President lacks that flexibility.”
Under Section 3 of the legislation, the President must first consult with the House Ways and Means and Foreign Affairs Committees, along with the Senate Finance and Foreign Relations Committees, and submit a report at least 45 days before providing the required certification.
Lawmakers have argued that the Administration has failed to follow this process.
“The President has to provide a certification to Congress in advance before lifting the prohibition,” says Eichensehr, pointing to the specific criteria set out in the wording of the law.
The law requires a determination by the President to Congress that the Russian Federation has withdrawn and ceased hostilities accepted by Ukraine; poses no immediate threat to any NATO member; and recognizes the right of the Ukrainian people to freely and independently choose their own government.
But Eichensehr insists that these are “not certifications that the President could make at the current moment” because “none of those things have happened, and that's the main restriction in the law.”
Even if all these conditions were met, the legislation would still require the President to wait an additional 90 days before the termination of the import ban could take effect, during which, Congress could enact a joint resolution of disapproval.
“On the substance, the President cannot, as a factual matter, make the certifications because Russia is still attacking Ukraine,” says Eichensehr. “As a procedural matter, [because he reportedly has not consulted Congress], he hasn't followed the process that the law sets out.”
Edward Swaine, a research professor at George Washington University Law School, suggests these restrictions were put in place to ensure that “when the President and the Treasury Secretary decide that circumstances have changed, they go back and explain this to Congress, and give it notice so that it can disagree.”
“The President is supposed to make this determination that Russia has withdrawn its forces and doesn't pose any further threat of aggression. These are fairly high standards,” he tells TIME, noting that the statue provides “Congress with adequate notice to allow it to generate a joint resolution of disapproval.”
“They don't want the President to be able to change this regime on a whim, and so I imagine Congress looking at this action and justifiably thinking that this is inconsistent,” he adds.
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has defended the legality of the agreement, insisting that the Trump Administration is acting within its existing legal authority to help bring energy prices down.
“We’re doing it with all the legal authorities we have, so anyone in Congress who says that—whether it’s an old bill or the current Lindsey Graham bill—prohibits us from doing it, is wrong,” he told Fox News on Sunday, without elaborating on which legal authorities he was referring to.
On Friday, the Treasury Department’s Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) issued a temporary general license authorizing transactions involving Russian diesel fuel, including its importation, until April 7, 2027.

articles.title_orig: David Cromer Will Direct Peter Friedman in Hanukkah Spectacular World Premiere
articles.title_zh: David Cromer Will Direct Peter Friedman in Hanukkah Spectacular World Premiere
articles.content_orig:
Max Posner's comedy will begin at the Woolly Mammoth Theatre in November.
October 13, 2026 By Andrew Gans
Washington , D.C.'s Woolly Mammoth Theatre Company will present the world premiere of Hanukkah Spectacular , a new comedy by Lucille Lortel Award nominee Max Posner, beginning November 14.
Directed by Tony winner David Cromer ( The Band's Visit , Dead Outlaw , The Sound Inside ), performances will continue through December 13.
Stage and screen star and Tony nominee Peter Friedman ( Succession, Ragtime , JOB ) will lead a cast that also includes Laura Heisler , Ben Edelman , Ben Beckley , and Ethan J. Miller.
Set over a long weekend at a Midtown talent agency, Hanukkah Spectacular follows a group of Jewish artists brought together to create a commercially viable holiday hit about Hanukkah.
“The first time I saw a reading of Hanukkah Spectacular three years ago, I knew I had just experienced something unforgettable, and I’m so lucky to get to share its world premiere with D.C. this holiday season,” says Woolly Mammoth Artistic Director Reggie D. White in a statement. “Seeing Max [Posner] and [David] Cromer collaborate feels like once-in-generation chemistry. Watching them amplify, interrogate, and deepen each other’s work is like you’re witnessing two brilliant artists write the book on collaboration in front of your very eyes. Max’s play is a hilarious and deeply recognizable story about a group of people trying to make something honest while figuring out what they actually believe. This production promises to be exactly the kind of work we come to the theatre to see: disarming, surprising, and so true that that it sends you back into the world thinking about your own life a little differently.”
Posner's play The Treasurer , also directed by Cromer, premiered at Playwrights Horizons and received a Lucille Lortel Award nomination for Best Play. He is a Sundance Institute Fellow, a recipient of the Helen Merrill Award and three MacDowell Fellowships, and was the 2024–25 Sun Valley Playwright-in-Residence at the Hemingway House.

articles.title_orig: OpenAI engineer arrested in bugging of executive conference room
articles.title_zh: OpenAI engineer arrested in bugging of executive conference room
articles.content_orig:
Federal prosecutors say an employee from Saudi Arabia planted an audio recorder and left another unattended in his bag.
An OpenAI engineer has been arrested on suspicion of hiding an audio recording device in an executive conference room at the company’s San Francisco headquarters, federal prosecutors said Tuesday.
Abdulrahman Alfozan, 35, a Saudi national, was arrested Friday and charged with using or attempting to use a device to intercept oral communications. He made his initial appearance in federal court Tuesday and remains in custody.
An unattended bag found in the company’s offices contained Alfozan’s wallet and identification, as well as a recording device, according to the U.S. attorney’s office in San Francisco.
Alfozan has worked as an engineer at OpenAI since July 2025, prosecutors said.
OpenAI personnel found the device Sept. 30. It was plugged into a USB port on the back of a television in an executive conference room and had been concealed in toilet paper, the complaint says. The company determined it was installed around Sept. 28, and its contents were encrypted.
Surveillance footage shows Alfozan near the room on multiple dates before the discovery, though he was not authorized to enter the room or attend meetings there, prosecutors said. Meetings in the room frequently involved confidential technical, commercial, and strategic information, including proprietary research, product plans, and government engagements, according to the complaint.
Before the device was installed, Alfozan used a productivity tool to ask about OpenAI’s building addresses, meeting rooms, room capacities, and calendars, as well as the locations of leadership and outside partner meetings, the complaint alleges.
A chatbot account tied to Alfozan’s spouse, which shared identifiers with his own account, submitted prompts between Sept. 24 and Sept. 30 about building, installing, obscuring, and remotely accessing a recording device, prosecutors said. Queries included how to “build a continuous audio recorder” and “encrypt the SD card,” prosecutors claimed. On Sept. 27 and 28, the account asked about the specific device that was later found, including its unique MAC address.
On Oct. 5, the complaint says, Alfozan entered the conference room and appeared to look behind the television. That same day, he allegedly left a bag unattended in a different room. Security personnel who opened it found his wallet and ID, along with a second recording device similar to the first.
“For us it is a matter of national security,” U.S. Attorney Craig Missakian said in a statement.
FBI Director Kash Patel said protecting U.S. AI innovation is among the bureau’s highest counterintelligence priorities. Scott Schelble, special agent in charge of the FBI’s San Francisco field office, said the agency is committed to protecting sensitive research and proprietary technology.
If convicted, Alfozan faces up to five years in prison and a $250,000 fine, followed by three years of supervised release.
The case is being prosecuted by the National Security, Cyber & Special Prosecutions Section of the U.S. attorney’s office for the Northern District of California.
OpenAI said on X (opens in new tab) that after discovering the device, employees used the company’s AI models to determine what it was and where it came from, and referred the matter to the FBI. The company thanked the agents and prosecutors who “moved quickly to make an arrest.”
According to OpenAI, its technical surveillance countermeasures team found the device during a sweep of a conference room.
OpenAI described the device as sophisticated and designed to evade detection, saying it had advanced encryption, audio monitoring capabilities, and a mechanism for transferring data in a way meant to avoid monitoring. The company said investigators used its models to analyze forensic images of the device’s storage and assess changes in the underlying data.
The company said it has evidence that Alfozan intended to place other recording devices in sensitive spaces to secretly record meetings.
According to OpenAI, Alfozan was a member of the product team. The company said it coordinated the timing of his firing with the FBI to avoid disrupting the investigation, and he was terminated Friday, the day he was arrested. Between Sept. 30 and that date, OpenAI said, it gradually restricted his access to systems and spaces, then suspended his physical and network access, placed him on leave, and secured his company-issued equipment.
A YouTube video last month touted him as the only Saudi employee at OpenAI.
“Honestly, this one year felt like five years anywhere else,” he said in response to a question about his experience.
“The idea of AI is that it handles things one might not want to do, so they can focus on tasks or hobbies they enjoy more or work they take pleaseure in and let it do the tedious tasks,” Alfozan said later in the video.
A LinkedIn profile that matches Alfozan’s name lists his OpenAI role as engineering lead on the company’s AI agents platform
Before joining OpenAI,  he was a founding engineer at Nash, an AI infrastructure company for logistics, from 2022 to August 2025, according to the LinkedIn profile. From 2017 to 2022, he was a senior systems engineer at Meta. His earlier experience, according to the profile, includes a stint as a systems engineer at Reach Labs, a wireless power startup in Y Combinator’s summer 2015 batch, and internships at Microsoft, SAP in Berlin and Akamai Technologies.
He has a master’s degree in data science from UC Berkeley, the LinkedIn profile says.
A man in the passenger seat of a car at Alfozan’s Millbrae home said that the family did not want to speak to reporters.
OpenAI said it has no indication that Alfozan improperly accessed or took model weights, source code, or customer data and has not seen activity that compromised the safety of its products or customers’ information. The company said it will continue to support the FBI’s investigation.
OpenAI said it treats protecting its technology, data and people “as a matter of national importance” and called the case an example of how AI can counter sophisticated security threats.
A detention hearing before U.S. Magistrate Judge Alex G. Tse is set for Oct. 19.
Michael is a deputy breaking news editor at The Standard.

articles.title_orig: How you can prepare for 6% bond yields
articles.title_zh: How you can prepare for 6% bond yields
articles.content_orig:
The yield on the 10-year Treasury fell on Thursday as traders digested comments from a top Federal Reserve official along with another long-dated bond auction.
The benchmark 10-year Treasury yield was down more than 4 basis points at 5.229% after reaching its highest level since 2002 this week. The 30-year Treasury bond yield dropped more than 5 basis points to 5.602% after trading around a 24-year high recently.
One basis point is equal to 0.01%, and yields and prices move in opposite directions.
Fed Governor Christopher Waller said on Thursday that more hikes are needed to bring inflation down after around 5-and-a-half years above the central bank's 2% target, but suggested rates did not need to rise immediately.
"The hikes do not need to come at consecutive meetings," Waller told a Central Bank of Turkey forum in Istanbul. "But they should be in place in an acceptable period of time."
His comments initially sent yields higher on the day. However, rates gave back those advances after President Donald Trump said the U.S. won't attack Iran until after the November midterm election . Yields also pulled back after a solid 30-year Treasury bond auction.
The department sold $22 billion in 30-year paper, with indirect bidders — which include central banks — scooping up 72.3% of the sale. That's above a 10-auction average of 68%. Direct bidders, including institutional investors, took 20.9% of the auction, just below an average of 22%. The yield at auction ease 5.618%.
That marks the final auction of the week. The department sold $58 billion in 3-year notes on Tuesday and another $39 billion in 10-year notes.
Thursday's sale "was decent but nowhere close to as good as the 10 yr auction yesterday," wrote Peter Boockvar, chief investment officer of One Point BFG Wealth Partners.
— CNBC's Brianna Bernath contributed reporting.

articles.title_orig: Peru governor touts Chinese interest in deep-water port pitched as Chancay alternative
articles.title_zh: Peru governor touts Chinese interest in deep-water port pitched as Chancay alternative
articles.content_orig:
Scaled back to US$844 million from a US$7 billion plan, Corio terminal in Arequipa has yet to secure an investor or operator
A planned US$844 million port in southern Peru has drawn interest from several foreign investors, including Chinese companies, a regional governor said on Monday, as the government began promoting the project abroad.
“Several companies have approached us. We have investors from the US, China and India who are very interested,” Rohel Sanchez, the governor of Arequipa, told reporters after signing an agreement with the state investment agency Proinversion.
He said firms from Turkey and the Netherlands had also been in touch, as had South Korean investors interested in technology for a logistics park to be built alongside the terminal.
Proinversion president Luis del Carpio said Corio would likely handle general cargo and containers but could also be used to export copper from the region to Asia.

articles.title_zh: Living World Seasons Are Now Included with Guild Wars 2 Expansions
articles.content_orig:
by The Guild Wars 2 Team on October 13, 2026
Over the past fourteen years, the story of Guild Wars 2 ® has been told across six expansions and five Living World™ seasons. While we’re proud of this extensive content library, we’re always looking for ways to improve how new and returning players access our adventures in Tyria. Today, we’re launching a series of updates to our expansion bundles and the Guild Wars 2 Starter Pack to increase their overall value, streamline our offerings, and introduce some major changes to how players access Living World content.
Here’s is a breakdown of what has changed:
For pricing, and to explore these new and updated offerings, visit our web store , the in-game store, Steam , and the Epic Games Store . Steam players can take advantage of Steam’s dynamic bundle pricing, automatically discounting based on content you already own.
Expansions are still available for purchase individually and if you’ve never played Living World Season 2, everyone can now experience it for free just by logging in!
If you purchased any Living World content after September 12, 2026, your account will automatically receive a gem refund equal to the value of that content. This also includes partial gem refunds for purchases of the Guild Wars 2 Elder Dragon Saga—Complete Collection. You will receive the full value of your Living World content, and the refund will be applied automatically to your account. If you do not receive your Guild Wars 2 Starter Pack items or Living World gem refund by October 15, please contact our Support team at support@arena.net .
Each bundle includes the Character Slots and Shared Inventory Slots that would normally come with their associated expansion. If you already own one or more expansions within a bundle, the associated Character Slots and Shared Inventory Slots will not be applied an additional time.
Our goal with these changes is to make jumping into Guild Wars 2 as seamless as possible. By increasing the value of our expansions and simplifying the purchasing options, we are making it easier than ever for new and returning players to dive into the vast, evolving world of Tyria.
